conbody.p: The trunk can be used to store the AC charging cable.
If the charging cable is dirty, clean it with a soft cloth soaked in a 3% neutral detergent solution, then wipe it dry with a clean cloth. Ensure it is fully dry in a well-ventilated, shaded area.
Avoid getting water on the charging connector and plug.

li.p: Do not modify or disassemble the charging cable as it poses a risk of fire, electric shock, and injury.
Always keep the charging connector and plug dry and clean. Store the charging cable without any moisture.
If there are any foreign objects or dust inside the charging connector or plug, remove them with an air gun.

Do not charge the vehicle if the charging connector or plug is damaged, corroded, rusty, or feels loose when connected. In this case, have your vehicle inspected by a professional workshop. Kia recommends visiting an authorized Kia dealer or service partner.
Do not pull the charging cable with excessive force.
Ensure the cable does not twist or kink.
Do not drag the cable on the ground.
Do not place objects on top of the cable.
Do not expose the cable to heat sources.
Do not drop the cable or subject it to strong impacts.
Do not store the cable with liquids or similar substances.
Do not use organic solvents like benzene, thinner, or detergents, as they can deform, discolor, or damage the charging cable.
When using general vehicle cleaners to clean the charging cable, ensure they do not contain organic solvents.
